raw_text:
Below is a 12-week, phase-based strength program designed for a 36-year-old recreational lifter returning from a right medial meniscus tear. The surgeon has cleared low-impact strength work with no jumping and no deep knee flexion under load. The goals are to rebuild lower-body strength and control, improve knee resilience, and set the foundation for next ski season. The program emphasizes bilateral and unilateral strength within safe ROM, robust hip and trunk stability, progressive loading, and tissue capacity while avoiding impact and excessive knee flexion angles.

Global structure
- Frequency: 3 strength days/week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri) + 1–2 optional accessory/conditioning sessions
- Sessions: ~60–75 minutes
- Lower-body ROM guardrails:
  - No loaded deep knee flexion past ~60–70° initially; progress ROM only if pain-free and with good control.
  - Use box height, safety pins, and tempo to control depth. Prioritize neutral knee tracking and even load through both legs.
- Warm-up (every session, 10–12 minutes):
  - 5 min easy bike or brisk incline walk
  - Dynamic mobility: ankle rocks (front/back), leg swings (front/side), hip airplanes (supported), T-spine openers
  - Knee/hip activation: terminal knee extensions (band TKE) 2×15/side; mini-band lateral walks 2×12/side; glute bridges 2×12
- Tempo, RPE, and progression:
  - Use controlled eccentrics (2–3 sec) on lower-body lifts early on to improve motor control
  - Progress load 2.5–5% weekly if all sets hit prescribed RPE with no knee symptoms (no pain >2/10, no swelling next day)
  - If pain/soreness >2/10 or lingering swelling: hold load, reduce ROM or volume by 20–30% for 1 week
- Conditioning (optional 1–2×/week): low-impact bike, elliptical, sled push/pull, or uphill treadmill walk; 20–30 min Zone 2
- Recovery: 7–8 hours sleep, post-session light bike 5 min, optional 5–10 min mobility, and quad/hamstring soft tissue work as tolerated
- Brace/Support: If client feels unstable, a light knee sleeve can be used for proprioception (not required)
- Return-to-ski specificity: Emphasize hip/quad endurance, lateral control, torso stiffness, and isometric holds; later add safe machine-based knee angles and anti-rotation core.

Key coaching points for the knee
- Prioritize hip hinge patterns and partial ROM squats with a box set to pain-free depth.
- Unilateral work: start supported and shallow; progress ROM, load, and independence gradually.
- Avoid twisting under load; emphasize alignment (knee tracks over 2nd–3rd toe).
- Use sled, leg press with limited ROM, and split stances to build quad strength without deep flexion.

Phase overview
- Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Reintroduction and base. Motor control, isometrics, partial ROM strength, lateral stability.
- Phase 2 (Weeks 4–6): Strength foundation. Increase bilateral loads, progress unilateral ROM, introduce machine-based knee angles.
- Phase 3 (Weeks 7–9): Strength intensification. Heavier hinges, more challenging split work, controlled eccentrics, isometric endurance.
- Phase 4 (Weeks 10–12): Strength consolidation and ski prep. Higher loads within safe ROM, lateral strength endurance, trunk stiffness, and capacity.

Weekly structure (each week: Day A, Day B, Day C). Where ROM is specified, use pain-free range and predetermined box/stop height.

Phase 1: Weeks 1–3 — Base, motor control, isometrics, safety ROM
Day A
- A1 Trap bar deadlift (high handles) to mid-shin, 3×6, tempo 3-1-1, RPE 6
- A2 Half-kneeling cable anti-rotation press (Pallof), 3×10/side
- B1 Box squat (box height above parallel; no bounce), 3×6–8, tempo 3-1-1, RPE 6
- B2 Supported split squat (front foot elevated 2–3 cm, shallow), 3×8/side, bodyweight or light DB, RPE 6
- C1 Hamstring slide-outs on towels/TRX (short range), 3×8
- C2 Standing calf raises, 3×12

Day B
- A1 Romanian deadlift (barbell or DB), 4×6, 3-1-1, RPE 6–7
- A2 Side plank with top-leg abduction (short lever if needed), 3×20–30 sec/side
- B1 Leg press (feet mid-sled, shoulder-width, limit depth to 60–70° knee flex), 3×8, RPE 6
- B2 Step-up to low box (controlled, no push-off from trail leg; right leg cautious), 3×6/side, RPE 6
- C1 Seated hamstring curl (short ROM if needed), 3×10
- C2 Seated soleus raises (knees at ~90°), 3×12–15

Day C
- A1 Hip thrust (barbell or machine), 4×6–8, 2-1-1, RPE 6–7
- A2 Tall-kneeling cable chop, 3×10/side
- B1 Goblet box squat (same box as Day A), 3×8, 3-1-1, RPE 6
- B2 Reverse lunge to box touch (rear knee to pad; short step to limit front-knee angle), 3×6/side, RPE 6
- C1 Sled push (light–moderate, flat), 4×20–25 m
- C2 Adductor side-lying leg lifts or Copenhagen short-lever, 3×10/side (start light)

Notes and progression week-to-week in Phase 1:
- Week 1: Establish ROM and loads (RPE 6). Emphasize tempo and alignment.
- Week 2: +2.5–5% load where smooth; keep ROM same.
- Week 3: Maintain load, increase ROM slightly if entirely pain-free (e.g., 1–2 cm lower box), or add 1 set on main movements if ROM unchanged.

Phase 2: Weeks 4–6 — Strength foundation, progressive ROM
Day A
- A1 Trap bar deadlift (high handles), 4×5, RPE 7
- A2 Half-kneeling anti-rotation press, 3×10/side (heavier)
- B1 Box squat (slightly lower if tolerated), 4×5, RPE 7
- B2 Bulgarian split squat to shallow depth (rear foot on low pad/step), 3×6/side, RPE 7
- C1 Hamstring slide-outs or Nordic eccentric to box (partial), 3×6–8
- C2 Standing calf raise, 3×10–12 with 2-sec pause at top

Day B
- A1 Barbell RDL, 4×5, RPE 7–8
- A2 Side plank with reach-through, 3×25–35 sec/side
- B1 Leg press (increase load, same ROM; feet slightly higher if needed), 4×6, RPE 7
- B2 Step-up to moderate box (still below knee height), 3×6/side, RPE 7 (hold DBs if stable)
- C1 Seated hamstring curl (increase ROM toward full as tolerated), 3×8–10
- C2 Seated soleus raise, 3×12–15 (add load)

Day C
- A1 Hip thrust (bar or machine), 4×5–6, RPE 7–8
- A2 Cable chop/lift, 3×8–10/side
- B1 Goblet box squat or safety bar box squat, 4×5–6, RPE 7
- B2 Reverse lunge to pad (slightly longer step as tolerated), 3×6/side, RPE 7
- C1 Sled push heavier, 5×20–25 m
- C2 Copenhagen plank short lever, 3×15–20 sec/side

Progression in Phase 2:
- Week 4: Introduce slightly lower box if symptom-free. Keep tempo 2–3 sec down.
- Week 5: +2.5–5% load; consider small ROM increase on unilateral work if no pain/swelling.
- Week 6: Consolidate strength—hold ROM, push load to RPE 7–8. If any knee irritability, reduce ROM and keep load.

Phase 3: Weeks 7–9 — Intensification, controlled eccentrics, unilateral capacity
Day A
- A1 Trap bar deadlift (high handles) or standard if ROM safe, 5×4, RPE 8
- A2 Pallof press iso-hold, 3×20–25 sec/side
- B1 Safety bar box squat (lowest safe box; still above parallel if needed), 5×4, RPE 8
- B2 Bulgarian split squat (ROM as tolerated), 3×5/side, 3-sec eccentric, RPE 7–8
- C1 Nordic curl eccentric to greater ROM (assist up), 3×4–6
- C2 Standing calf raise heavy, 4×8–10

Day B
- A1 Barbell RDL or rack pull (just below knee if back needs), 5×4, RPE 8
- A2 Side plank with band row, 3×8–10/side
- B1 Leg press (heavier within ROM), 5×5, RPE 8
- B2 Step-downs from low box (controlled, tap and up), 3×6/side, 3-sec eccentric
- C1 Seated hamstring curl heavy, 3×6–8
- C2 Seated soleus raise heavy, 4×10–12

Day C
- A1 Hip thrust heavy, 5×4–5, RPE 8
- A2 Anti-rotation walkout, 3×6–8 steps/side
- B1 Front-foot-elevated split squat (small elevation) to tolerance, 3×5/side, RPE 7–8
- B2 Sled push/pull heavy, 6×20 m
- C1 Copenhagen plank medium lever, 3×20–25 sec/side
- C2 Adductor machine or side-lying adduction, 3×10–12

Progression in Phase 3:
- Week 7: Move to RPE 8 loads with strict control.
- Week 8: +2.5% load or 1 extra set on main lift if bar speed/quality good.
- Week 9: Maintain load; test slightly lower box/greater ROM if 100% symptom-free. If any twinge, revert to prior ROM.

Phase 4: Weeks 10–12 — Consolidation, ski-specific strength endurance and trunk stiffness
Emphasis: maintain heavier bilateral strength; add quasi-isometrics and longer time-under-tension for quads and adductors; lateral/resistance to valgus; avoid impact.

Day A
- A1 Trap bar deadlift heavy, 4×3–4, RPE 8–8.5
- A2 Pallof press march, 3×8/side
- B1 Safety bar box squat heavy, 4×3–4, RPE 8–8.5 (ROM as established)
- B2 Wall sit with heel pressure (no deep angle; choose ~60–70°), 3×30–45 sec
- C1 Nordic eccentrics or hamstring bridge iso, 3×20–30 sec
- C2 Standing calf raise with isometric top hold, 3×8 + 10-sec hold each set

Day B
- A1 RDL heavy, 4×3–4, RPE 8–8.5
- A2 Side plank long lever, 3×25–35 sec/side
- B1 Leg press cluster sets: 3×(3+3+3) with 15-sec intra-set rest; ROM safe; RPE 8 across
- B2 Lateral sled drags (constant tension), 4×12–15 m/side
- C1 Seated hamstring curl, 3×6–8 heavy then 1×12 back-off
- C2 Seated soleus raise, 4×10–12

Day C
- A1 Hip thrust heavy, 4×3–4, RPE 8–8.5
- A2 Cable chop/lift alternating, 3×8/side
- B1 Split squat pattern (choose best tolerated: Bulgarian, front-foot-elevated, or regular), 4×5/side, RPE 8 (3-sec eccentric first 2 sets)
- B2 Isometric lateral lunge hold to short depth (no deep knee angle), 3×20–30 sec/side, push hips back, knee tracking clean
- C1 Sled push moderate, 5×25–30 m continuous
- C2 Copenhagen plank medium/long lever, 3×25–35 sec/side

Progression in Phase 4:
- Week 10: Establish near-top working loads within safe ROM.
- Week 11: Small load increase or add 1 set to a main movement.
- Week 12: Slight deload mid-week to consolidate (reduce volume by ~20% on Days B/C) while keeping intensity similar; finish week with quality reps and strong positions.

Accessory/finisher (optional, 1–2×/week, keep low-impact)
- Quad endurance: 2–3 rounds of 45–60 sec continuous leg extension partials in safe ROM (if comfortable), light–moderate load
- Core/anti-rotation circuit: Pallof variations, farmer’s carries (suitcase), dead bug with band, 2–3 rounds

Mobility and tissue care (5–10 minutes post-session or off days)
- Quad/hip flexor stretch (cushioned), 2×30–45 sec
- Hamstring stretch (gentle), 2×30 sec
- Adductor rocking in quadruped, 2×8–10
- Ankle dorsiflexion mobilizations, 2×10/side
- Patellar tendon and quad soft tissue with light rolling as tolerated

Conditioning guidance
- Weeks 1–4: Bike or elliptical 20–25 min, Zone 2, 1–2×/week
- Weeks 5–8: 25–30 min; include 4–6 × 60-sec moderate efforts with 90-sec easy (no impact)
- Weeks 9–12: 30 min steady or sled intervals 6–8 × 30–40 m with walk-back

Pain/response criteria and modifications
- Green light: 0–2/10 discomfort during or after, no next-day swelling/stiffness increase.
- Yellow: 3–4/10 or next-day swelling—reduce ROM, switch to machine-based option (leg press) or isometric variant, cut volume by 20–30%.
- Red: >4/10 pain, catching/locking, or swelling spike—stop loaded knee flexion work that day, replace with hinges/hip thrusts and isometrics; notify surgeon/PT if persistent.

Weekly snapshot (condensed)
- Week 1: Establish ROM, light loads, tempo control.
- Week 2: Small load increases, same ROM.
- Week 3: Slight ROM progress if symptom-free.
- Week 4: Heavier within ROM, introduce SSB/goblet progressions.
- Week 5: Progress loads 2.5–5%, unilateral depth cautiously.
- Week 6: Consolidate; sled heavier.
- Week 7: Intensify to RPE 8; eccentrics 3-sec on unilateral.
- Week 8: Add a set or slight load bump; monitor knee response.
- Week 9: Maintain intensity; explore minor ROM increases only if perfect.
- Week 10: Top-end strength within safe angles; add isometric endurance.
- Week 11: Small progression or extra set; lateral drags/holds continue.
- Week 12: Slight volume taper mid-week; finish strong with quality.

Nutrition and recovery (brief)
- Protein: ~1.6–2.2 g/kg/day; distribute across 3–4 meals with 25–40 g high-quality protein each
- Carbs: Support training with 1–2 g/kg around sessions; include a carb + protein meal within 2 hours post-workout
- Hydration: 30–35 ml/kg/day; add electrolytes if sweating heavily
- Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day
- Omega-3s: 1–2 g EPA/DHA if dietary intake is low
- Bodyweight: Maintain or slight surplus if strength gain is priority; avoid aggressive deficits during rehab

Return-to-ski transition after Week 12
- Maintain 2 strength sessions/week (one bilateral-heavy, one unilateral/lateral-focused)
- Add ski-specific conditioning: longer Zone 2 rides 35–45 min, plus low-impact intervals; progress to slideboard and controlled lateral skater steps without jump on approval
- When cleared for deeper knee flexion, gradually reintroduce depth on squats/leg press over 4–6 weeks before any plyometric return.

This plan respects the no-jumping and limited deep knee flexion constraints, builds comprehensive lower-body and trunk strength, and progressively targets the qualities needed for a confident return to skiing.
